- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment >0.8) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment remains high.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing: if sentiment changes by >0.3 in 3–5 days, adjust forecast by -0.1 to -0.3 of previous day’s deviation.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.8 → 0.1 → 0.8), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true reversal point.
